title: fix(data-objectstack): the entry-form filter refuses an empty or non-string icontains comparand, reading the spec's own predicate (objectui#9048)
body:
Fixes #9048
Clause-②: no

## What this lands

This is the open half of maintainer ruling D (comment `5658597078`, decision batch #133 item 1). The ruling asks for one implementation and three envelopes. `objectFilterEntryToAST` is the rule-entry arm of `translateFilterArray`. It now asks `@objectstack/spec/data`'s `isRefusedTextComparand` after `toAstFilterOperator`'s fold. On a refusal it throws `MalformedFilterError` (`INVALID_FILTER` / 400) carrying `textComparandRefusalReason(field, ARRIVED_SPELLING, value)` byte for byte, and it throws before any request is sent. The three envelopes are now:

- `FilterOperatorError` from `convertFiltersToAST` and `viewFilterRuleToNode`;
- exclude-and-log in `ValueDataSource`;
- `MalformedFilterError` here.

All three read the spec's two functions. ⛔ No new export from `@object-ui/core`.

- **The door sits in `objectFilterEntryToAST` itself**, so every caller meets it:
  - both `find()` routes, plain and `$expand`;
  - `exportDownload`;
  - `aggregate()`'s analytics lowering;
  - a nested rule group;
  - a bare rule spread under `and` / `or`. A bare rule now carries its position in the parent array as the index, which is why `translateFilterChild` gained an `index` argument.
- **The message names the spelling that arrived**, for example `ICONTAINS`. The tail names the `$`-dialect twin `'$icontains'`, so the row's `mustMention` holds. This is the seating `viewFilterRuleToNode` already uses for the same vocabulary.
- **`MalformedFilterError`'s published signature is unchanged.** The built `.d.ts` / `.d.cts` are byte-identical to BASE `e978ed5ea`, and a control on the round-0 head shows the instrument sees a difference. The refusal is an ordinary `MalformedFilterError`, built by the module-private `refuseTextComparandEntry`, which replaces its message with the refusal sentence. So `instanceof`, `name`, `code` `INVALID_FILTER` and `httpStatus` 400 are the class's own. The constructor's entry serialisation goes through a module-private describer that is BigInt- and cycle-safe, and its output is byte-identical for every entry that serialised before. (Patch round 1, answering contract review `5908617443`.)
- **An absent `value` gets no carve-out.** The stored-view lowering has one because it emits a 2-tuple for a valueless operator. This translator always emits a 3-tuple, so an absent value went out as JSON `null`, which is a non-string comparand (the table's second row). `ValueDataSource` refuses the same rule.

## Premises re-measured at BASE `e978ed5ea` (installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0)

- `packages/core/src/utils/text-comparand.ts` re-exports both functions from `@objectstack/spec/data`. The only other `isRefusedTextComparand` / `textComparandRefusalReason` hits in `core` are call sites and one pin that reads them. Verified, ⛔ not redone.
- The spec ROOT entry has no such functions (`typeof require('@objectstack/spec').isRefusedTextComparand` reads `undefined`); the `/data` subpath has both (`function`). This PR imports from `/data`, as `core` does.
- `@object-ui/data-objectstack` already declares `"@objectstack/spec": "^17.5.0"` directly. There is no manifest or lockfile change. `pnpm check:spec-floors` fetched 17.5.0 and inspected this package's built `dist`, which now imports both names from `@objectstack/spec/data`, with no finding.
- `FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES` has exactly one row whose value is `icontains`, the identity row. Case variants fold through `toLowerCase`. `$icontains`, `containsCaseInsensitive` and `i_contains` do not fold; they pass through raw, before and after this change.

## Before and after, measured by a throwaway probe driving `find()` (deleted, not committed)

Both routes gave identical answers, so they are shown once.

| input | BASE `e978ed5ea` | this branch |
|:--|:--|:--|
| entry `icontains`, `''` | sent `["name","icontains",""]` | `MalformedFilterError` INVALID_FILTER/400, nothing sent |
| entry `icontains`, `42` / `null` / `true` / `["a"]` / `{}` | sent verbatim | refused, nothing sent |
| entry `icontains`, `value` absent | sent `["name","icontains",null]` | refused, nothing sent |
| entry `ICONTAINS` / `iContains` / `IContains` / `op:` key, `''` | sent | refused, naming the spelling that arrived |
| bare rule under `and`; nested rule group | sent | refused (entry 1 / entry 0) |
| entry `icontains`, `'acme'` (CONTROL) | `["name","icontains","acme"]` | unchanged |
| entry `contains`, `''` (SCOPE) | `["name","contains",""]` | unchanged: the table declares no row for it |
| object `{ name: { $icontains: '' } }` / `42` | refused (objectui#9001) | unchanged |
| `ValueDataSource`, same entry filter, each comparand above | refuses all except `'acme'` | unchanged, and now the adapter agrees |

## Tests (round 0, HEAD `d7bd5a111`; the patch-round readings at the final head `26de698a1` are in the next section)

All runs are from the worktree root, under `os-verify-lock.sh`. Pass COUNTS are read, not exit codes.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/data-objectstack/ scripts/__tests__/spec-symbol-ledger-data-objectstack-7265.test.ts`: **Test Files 74 passed (74), Tests 1017 passed (1017)**, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- The new pin file, `packages/data-objectstack/src/filter-entry-text-comparand-9048.test.ts`: **52 passed (52)**. It covers:
  - the spec's own rejection rows, derived from `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` with each row's `code` and `mustMention` asserted;
  - `''` and `42` refused, with `'acme'` as the control;
  - every spelling the alias table folds to `icontains`, plus two case variants, each paired with its own control;
  - the object form and the entry form refusing the same node with one reason;
  - a verdict-for-verdict parity table against `ValueDataSource` over nine comparands;
  - index naming at depth;
  - `aggregate()`;
  - a BigInt comparand, driven through `aggregate()`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/data-objectstack type-check`: exit 0, run after `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/data-objectstack^...' build`. `tsc --noEmit --listFiles` includes the new test file.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/data-objectstack build`: exit 0.
- The whole root `scripts/__tests__/` suite ran once because the diff adds a markdown changeset. It ran in three chunks whose union equals the 179-file population read from `git ls-tree` at HEAD: 177 files passed and 2 were skipped by design (the network-escape fixtures, inert outside the pin that spawns them); 5371 tests passed and 2 were skipped. `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit`: exit 0.
- Gates, each exit captured before any pipe, all **exit 0**:
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` ("2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)");
  - `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`;
  - `pnpm check:new-line-citations` ("0 new citation(s)"), `check:control-bytes`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unused-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:test-path-roots`.
- **NOT MEASURED, prerequisite not met.** `pnpm check:readme-exports` (exit 1) and `pnpm check:spec-floors` (exit 1) both went red only on sibling packages whose `dist/` is not built here. The first reports 480 self-imports it could not judge; the second reports 17 `[no-artifact]` findings. This package itself was judged by both, with no finding (README rows: 0 unjudged, 0 wrong-path, 0 fabricated). The full reading is CI's.

**Ablation**, on the committed fix (HEAD `75db0a505`). The direction was predicted before running: 37 red and 15 green, where the 15 are the two derivation guards plus every control or scope pin.

- The mutation went through `ablation-replace.mjs`, which disabled the guard's condition. The anchor fell from 1 to 0 and the blob moved from `d4ad4247` to `92aaf4e2`.
- The pin file read **37 failed, 15 passed (52)**, exactly as predicted, and none of the 37 was a control, scope or derivation pin.
- The restore was proven by state: the blob went back to `d4ad4247` (equal to HEAD), `git diff HEAD` was empty, and the marker count was 0.
- The subject is imported relatively (`./index`), so it resolves to source and no `dist` staleness applies.

**Lint, a declared narrowing.** The package's `lint` is `eslint .` resolving the root flat config. That config lints `**/*.{ts,tsx}`, and this diff adds or changes exactly two such files.

- `pnpm exec eslint --format json` over both files at HEAD `d7bd5a111` read 2 files and 0 errors. The new test has 0 warnings. `index.ts` has 123 `no-explicit-any` warnings, the same count as BASE `index.ts` linted through stdin.
- Invariance: type-aware linting is not enabled. The config extends `tseslint.configs.recommended`, not a type-checked variant, and `languageOptions` carries only `ecmaVersion` and `globals`, with no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`.
- No local rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem: a grep for `fs` reads matched no rule file, while the same grep matched a positive control. So this diff cannot move a verdict on any file it does not contain.

## Patch round 1 (final head `26de698a1`), answering contract review `5908617443`

- **Finding 1 (semver).** Fixed by option B: `MalformedFilterError`'s published constructor is back to `(entry, index)`, and the built `.d.ts` / `.d.cts` are byte-identical to BASE (0 diff lines; the control on `d7bd5a111` differs). This keeps `'@object-ui/data-objectstack': patch` and `Clause-②: no`.
- **Finding 2 (README).** "Rule-shaped arrays" now says an `icontains` entry whose value is empty, a number, `null` or missing throws `MalformedFilterError` (`INVALID_FILTER` / 400) before any request, naming the spelling that arrived. The export-listing comment is widened to match.
- **Readings at `26de698a1`:**
  - `vitest packages/data-objectstack/` plus the spec-symbol ledger: 74 files, 1019 tests. The pin file has 54 tests.
  - Ablation leg A (the guard): 37 red / 17 green. Leg B (the BigInt-safe describer): 2 red / 52 green. Both were predicted in advance.
  - The root `scripts/__tests__` suite is green, and `markdown-test-inputs --audit` exits 0.
  - CI: 43 runs, 40 success, 3 expected skips, 0 failure.

## Acceptance notes

These are recorded rather than filed: none has a demonstrated public entrance or named producer.

- **An AST tuple is still passed through unjudged.** `$filter: ['name','icontains','']` reaches the wire unchanged, both before and after this change. `translateFilterArray` deliberately leaves an already-lowered comparison tuple for the server ("the server decides"). `ValueDataSource`'s AST arm refuses the same tuple. The in-tree AST producers `convertFiltersToAST` and `toFilterNode` both refuse the shape first. Owner: none.
- **`find()` throws a bare `TypeError` when its params hold a BigInt.** The throw comes from its request-coalescing key (`stableStringify(params)`), before any translation, and for any operator, `contains` included. No JSON-sourced filter can carry a BigInt. Owner: none.
- **objectui#9050 is untouched, per the ruling.** Where render-time `toFilterNode` throws surface remains that card's decision.
